timberline-hdz-charcoal.title: GAF Timberline HDZ Charcoal Shingles
timberline-hdz-charcoal.description: Architectural laminate shingles in deep charcoal, featuring LayerLock technology that considerably widens the nailing zone for a faster, surer fastening.
about: Timberline HDZ (GAF) is the best selling GAF shingle, a fiberglass asphalt architectural shingle shown here in Charcoal, one of its High Definition colors. LayerLock Technology powers StrikeZone, the largest nailing zone in the industry, and Dura Grip thermal sealant bonds the shingles together once they are exposed to sun and warm temperatures, so they stay in place under high wind. It meets ASTM D3462 and is rated Class A for fire.

Each shingle measures 13 1/4 x 39 3/8 in (337 x 1,000 mm) with a 5 5/8 in (143 mm) exposure. A square takes 64 pieces in 3 bundles. GAF matches it with TimberTex or TimberCrest ridge cap and Pro Start, QuickStart or WeatherBlocker starter strips at eaves and rakes. Install on slopes of 2:12 or greater over a deck of at least 3/8 in (10 mm) plywood or OSB. From 2:12 to under 4:12 the deck takes two layers of GAF Roof Deck Protection; at 4:12 and above, one.

Use zinc coated steel or aluminum roofing nails of 10 to 12 gauge with 3/8 to 7/16 in (10 to 12 mm) heads, long enough to penetrate 3/4 in (19 mm) into the deck, driven flush. The standard pattern is 4 nails about 6 7/8 in (174 mm) from the bottom of the shingle; some codes require 6. Mansard roofs of 21:12 and above are nailed 6 in (152 mm) from the bottom and hand sealed with 4 dabs of shingle tab adhesive.

Warranty: Lifetime coverage against manufacturing defects for the original owner of a single family home, or an eligible second owner. The 15 year WindProven Limited Wind Warranty, with no maximum wind speed, applies to LayerLock shingles installed with the required GAF starter strips, roof deck protection and other qualifying GAF accessories. StainGuard Plus adds a 25 year limited algae warranty using time release algae fighting technology.

brakki-10pc.title: Grey Ribbed Steel Panels 10 Pack
brakki-10pc.description: Grey ribbed galvanized steel roofing panels supplied as a ten piece package covering approximately seventy five square feet, screws included.
about: Brakki sells these panels as a ready to fit pack rather than as a factory run cut to your roof, so a small building arrives complete in one delivery. The sheets are ribbed galvanized steel in grey, each one measuring 61.02 x 17.72 in (1,550 x 450 mm), and ten come in the box. Grooved side edges interlock, which keeps the seam tight and makes the sheets quicker to line up on a frame. Nothing has to be cut or formed on site at all.

The ten piece pack covers 75.3 sq ft in total, which is the gross sheet area rather than the net area once the sheets overlap, so allow for the side and end laps when you work out how many packs a roof needs. Steel thickness is 0.01 in (0.25 mm). Fifty screws ship in the box, five per sheet, along with a pair of gloves for handling the cut edges safely. Brakki offers the same profile in a ten piece pack when the job is bigger.

Brakki lists the panels for garages, chicken coops, sheds, stables and patio covers, which is the work a light gauge sheet is meant for. They fasten straight through the flat of the profile into timber or steel purlins using the screws supplied. Lay each sheet so it laps the groove of the one before it, work from the eave upward, and keep the laps turned away from the prevailing wind. A cordless driver with a hex socket is the only tool needed.

Galvanizing is what carries the corrosion resistance here, and Brakki rates the finish as UV resistant and colourfast so the grey holds up in full sun. At 0.01 in this is a light gauge sheet built for outbuildings, not a substitute for a structural roof panel on a house. No warranty term, wind rating or fire classification is published for the pack, so treat it as accessory grade. Check local code before putting it over habitable space.

brakki-stone-tiles.title: DECRA Stone Coated Steel Roof Tiles
about: DECRA Tile is a pressure formed steel panel finished with a ceramic coated stone chip surface, so a roof reads as Mediterranean clay tile while weighing a fraction of it. The steel is aluminium zinc alloy coated to ASTM A792 at 26 gauge, 0.0179 in (0.455 mm), and each panel is pre corrugated into several vertical tiles forming one tile step across its face. The colour comes from the stone granules rather than a paint film that could chalk.

Each panel measures 16 1/2 x 52 in (419 x 1,321 mm) and installs to an exposure of 14 1/2 x 50 in (368 x 1,270 mm), which works out at twenty panels to the square. Installed weight is 150 lb per 100 sq ft, roughly a seventh of what concrete tile puts on the same structure, so DECRA Tile is often the option on a reroof where the frame cannot take more load. Matching valley, side and roof to wall flashings are pressed from the same 26 gauge steel.

Minimum slope is 3:12. Between 2:12 and 3:12 the deck takes an additional underlayment layer before the battens go down. The panel is listed for batten installation under ICC-ES report ESR-2901 and Florida approval FL9759-R9. Panels nail through the batten rather than face fixing, so no fastener head is left exposed to weather on the finished roof. Battens may be timber or steel, and counter battens are an option where drainage needs it.

Warranty: lifetime limited on a single family detached home, covering blow off in wind speeds up to 120 mph and hail stone penetration, cracking or splitting up to a 2.5 in stone. The system carries ASTM E108 and UL 790 Class A for fire and UL 2218 Class 4 for impact, which is the top impact class and often earns an insurance discount. Fasteners follow ANSI/ASME B18.6.1 for wood screws and B18.6.4 for thread forming tapping screws.

brakki-insulated-panel.title: Isodomus Insulated Sandwich Panel
about: Isodomus is an insulated sandwich panel from Isopan that arrives as a finished roof in one piece: a pressed steel outer sheet in a barrel tile shape, a rigid polyurethane core and a second steel sheet on the inside. One panel replaces tile, batten and insulation at once, which is why it turns up on rural and public buildings where a tiled look is required but the structure is light. Isopan makes the range in Italy in colours that imitate traditional tile.

The useful covering width is 1,000 mm and the tile pattern repeats on a 350 mm module with a profile height of 50 mm. The outer sheet is 0.5 mm steel and the inner sheet 0.4 mm, with a 0.6 mm aluminium outer face offered as an alternative. Core thicknesses start at 30 mm and rise from there, and working length is held to a tolerance of plus or minus 2 mm under EN 14509. Catalogue weight tables are given separately for steel and mono faced versions.

Fixing is the penetrating type, driven through the panel with exposed caps, and the number and position of the fasteners has to be worked out from the loads on the roof rather than taken as a fixed pattern. Minimum slope is seven percent. Published load tables run from a 1,050 mm span up to 3,500 mm, so the purlin spacing follows the core thickness chosen. Counter battens are not part of the system, so drainage is handled by the panel profile itself.

Thermal transmittance runs from 0.55 W/m2K on the thinnest core down to 0.19 W/m2K on the thickest, calculated to EN ISO 6946 and declared under UNI EN 14509:2007. The panel is light enough to help on seismic loads and fast enough to close a roof in a day, which is where most of its value sits on a refurbishment job. Isopan also lists a Classic version of the same panel with a different tile step running across its visible face.

certainteed-roofrunner.title: RoofRunner Underlayment
certainteed-roofrunner.description: Scrim reinforced synthetic underlayment covering ten squares, offering a slip resistant walking surface for safer work across steep wet decks.
about: RoofRunner is CertainTeed's lightweight synthetic polymer underlayment, built as a scrim reinforced sheet that goes down on the roof deck as a water resistant layer beneath asphalt shingles. A top surface treatment gives it grip that holds even when the sheet is wet, which is the part crews notice first, and the wide roll cuts the number of courses needed to dry in a plane. CertainTeed places it above felt and other synthetics in its own line.

The roll measures 48 in wide by 250 ft long and holds 1,000 sq ft of material. Once the side and end laps are taken out, net coverage works out at 937.5 sq ft, so roughly six percent of the roll goes into the overlaps. Each roll weighs 23 lb, light enough to carry up a ladder in one hand, and a pallet takes 56 of them. The sheet is 4 ft wide, so each course dries a 4 ft band of deck. A pallet therefore carries about 52,500 sq ft of net coverage.

It is fastened with standard roofing nails and is compatible with most asphalt shingles, with the underlayment warranty tracking whatever coverage period the shingle carries. CertainTeed rates it for up to 90 days of ultraviolet exposure, a figure drawn from standard accelerated QUV testing rather than from time actually spent uncovered on a roof. CertainTeed lists it as a water resistant layer rather than a waterproofing membrane.

It satisfies the physical requirements of both ASTM D226 and ASTM D4869, the two specifications written for asphalt saturated felt, which is the comparison most inspectors reach for. It carries UL 790 and ASTM E108 Class A fire resistance when paired with a Class A shingle, is listed under ICC-ES AC188 and holds Florida Approval FL 21841. Both ASTM figures cover the physical requirements only, not a fire or wind rating of their own.

protect-a1.title: Protect A1 Type HR Roofing Underlay
protect-a1.description: Vapour impermeable underlay keeping the roof airtight and watertight beneath tiles, supplied in generous rolls reaching forty five metres long.
about: Protect A1 is a Type HR impermeable roof underlay produced in the United Kingdom. A polypropylene non woven layer is coated on one face with a continuous film of polypropylene and polyethylene blend, and the sheet is black top and bottom with print on the upper face as installed. It is UKCA and CE marked, independently approved by BM TRADA and carries a Q Mark certification. It was developed to get past the drawbacks of Type 1F and 5U felts.

Mass is 145 g per square metre at a thickness of 0.6 mm, and it comes as 1 m by 45 m or 1.5 m by 30 m rolls. Water vapour transmission resistance is 112 MNs per gram, an Sd of 22 m, to BS EN ISO 12572, which satisfies the permeability that BM TRADA and the NHBC recommend. It stays flexible at low temperature and resists tearing at the nails. Thickness and mass are held across both roll formats. It also resists damage from handling on site.

Wind uplift use is unrestricted across the United Kingdom and Ireland, Zones 1 to 5, under BS 5534:2018, and at a batten gauge of 345 mm or less the sheet resists 1,732 Pa of wind pressure. Nail tear strength is 230 N along the roll and 234 N across it to BS EN 12310-1, while tensile strength reaches 287 N and 274 N to BS EN 12311-1. Both figures are measured with the modifications named in the standards. It is a secondary layer, never the roof itself.

Because it is a high resistance underlay, extra ventilation is required to BS 5250: a warm roof wants 25,000 mm² per metre at the eaves and 5,000 at the ridge, and a cold roof 10,000 at the eaves and 5,000 at the ridge behind a well sealed ceiling. Resistance to water penetration to BS EN 1928 with modifications is a pass at Class W1. A separate vapour control layer goes on the warm side of the insulation. Dust ingress is held back as well.

exoperm-mono.title: Exoperm Mono 150 Breather Membrane
exoperm-mono.description: Highly breathable monolithic membrane serving as sarking, roof underlay and windtight barrier across seventy five square metres per single roll.
about: Exoperm Mono 150 from Partel is a three ply sarking membrane whose middle layer is monolithic rather than microporous, so vapour crosses it by molecular diffusion instead of through pores that dirt or surfactants could block. It works as sarking, as a roof underlay and as a windtight barrier, on pitched roofs and on timber frame walls alike. The three plies are laminated so the functional layer sits protected between two covers.

One roll is 1.5 m by 50 m and covers 75 m², which is 807 sq ft, at a mass of 150 g per square metre measured to EN 1849-2. The vapour diffusion resistance is an Sd of just 0.07 m to EN ISO 12572 method C, among the most open figures published for a roofing membrane, while air permeance stays below 0.001 cubic metres per square metre hour. Partel measures both figures on the finished membrane rather than on the functional layer alone.

Water resistance is Class W1 to EN 1928, and Partel publishes that class as holding both before and after artificial ageing, which is the part that matters over a long build programme. Tensile strength is 255 N in the machine direction and 145 N across it per 50 mm to EN 12311-1, and nail tear resistance is 130 N and 160 N to EN 12310-1. Both strengths are quoted per 50 mm of width, the convention in the European standards.

The membrane holds its properties from 40 degrees below zero up to 80 degrees Celsius. Partel rates ultraviolet exposure at six months on a wall and four months on a roof, so it can sit open through a winter if the cladding slips. bmi-chova.title: Politaber Combi 40/G SBS Membrane
bmi-chova.description: Torch applied elastomeric membrane finished with mineral granules, supplied in rolls that individually cover ten square meters of flat roofing.
about: Politaber Combi 40/G is a modified bitumen sheet from ChovA, an LBM designated LBM-40/G-FP by AENOR. Bitumen modified with SBS elastomers sits on a reinforced non woven polyester felt, the underside is finished with plastic film and the face carries mineral granules or slate. It is bonded to the deck with a torch, and one edge is a printed 8 cm overlap band. The sheet leaves the factory free of visible defects under EN 1850-1.

kovertech-gold.title: KoverTech Gold Aluminum Membrane
kovertech-gold.description: Asphalt membrane topped with embossed aluminum that reflects solar radiation and resists cracking, covering approximately ten square meters per roll.
about: KoverTech Gold is built in four layers. The face is embossed aluminium foil 36 microns thick, under it sits a central reinforcement of high density polyethylene at 50 microns, then the body of plastic asphalt drawn from polymer modified bituminous bases with thermoplastic polymers, and the underside carries a polyethylene anti adhesive film that comes off as the sheet is torched. KoverTech names the grade Gold for that aluminium face.

A roll weighs 45 kg and covers about 10 m² at 1 m by 10 m. The embossed face is the point of the product: it reflects a good part of the solar radiation that would otherwise be absorbed, which keeps the membrane and the space under it cooler, and the foil lets the sheet stay exposed to ultraviolet light rather than needing a covering. The maker credits it with greater flexibility, more elongation and better mechanical resistance than its plainer lines.

It goes onto slabs, vaults, galvanised sheet and fibre cement roofs, and flat or domed roofs at any pitch. The substrate has to be clean, smooth and uniform, and it takes a coat of asphalt primer or emulsion first. Roll it transverse to the slope, following the direction water runs, and torch the underside with continuous pressure as it goes down. Any pitch is accepted as long as the water has somewhere to go. The film releases as the flame passes.

Overlaps run 8 to 10 cm between rolls, and terminations are doubled with at least 15 cm of overlap. One limit matters more than any other here: it must never go under a cement, lime and sand screed, because contact between those materials and the aluminium oxidises the foil and breaks the membrane down. It is not walkable once laid. No wind uplift figure, fire class or warranty term is published for it. It is sold by the roll, not the square metre.

ormiflex-profesional.title: Ormiflex Profesional Aluminum Membrane
ormiflex-profesional.description: Reinforced asphalt membrane faced with aluminum foil, rolled out and torched over inaccessible flat decks, covering roughly ten square meters.

So the line name printed on the roll tells you the gauge of the foil you are buying.

The Profesional line is sold in 10 m² rolls, marked by a coloured tape at the end: red tape for the 40 kg presentation and yellow tape for the 35 kg one, which is the roll offered here. gaf-everguard-tpo-quick-spray-7792.title: EverGuard TPO Quick Spray Adhesive
gaf-everguard-tpo-quick-spray-7792.description: Pressurised canister of solvent contact adhesive covering ten squares of smooth TPO membrane, sprayable down to twenty degrees Fahrenheit ambient.
about: A bucket and roller is a slow way to move adhesive around a roof, and on a large deck the slowness compounds: every pail is opened, stirred, poured, walked and rolled, and each of those steps is a place where the coverage rate quietly drifts away from what the specification says it should be. A canister and a gun turns all of that into pulling a trigger. The specification assumes a rate that the bucket almost never delivers.

This one holds ten squares, a thousand square feet, at 40.15 lb for the canister. It is a solvent based contact adhesive, so both the substrate and the underside of the membrane are sprayed and both are left to flash off until they feel tacky rather than wet. The membrane then goes down and is pressed home with a push broom and a weighted roller. A contact adhesive only works once both faces have properly flashed off, not before.

The number that puts it in the winter kit is the installation temperature: 20°F and rising, which is a long way below what a bucket adhesive will tolerate. The catch is that the canister itself has to stay above 50°F to spray properly, so in cold weather it travels in a hot box or under a heated blanket, and it must never be taken above 150°F. A cold canister does not spray properly; it dribbles, and the coverage rate goes with it.

GAF require their own hose and gun, SKU 7804 or 7805, because those carry the 11002 spray tip that produces the coverage rate the approvals were tested at, and because a shared gun risks contamination with another maker's adhesive. Spray from 8 to 12 inches out. VOC is 489 g/L, shelf life is two years, and the canister ships on its own. The hose, the gun and the cleaner are each ordered separately from the canister itself, which is worth knowing.

gaf-olybond-500.title: OlyBond500 Canister Adhesive Kit
gaf-olybond-500.description: Two component polyurethane foam adhesive that beads insulation board onto the deck, covering approximately thirty five squares per complete kit.
about: Every screw through an insulation board is a hole through the thermal layer and a small bridge for heat to cross. Multiply that by the fastener pattern across a whole commercial deck and the insulation quietly underperforms the number on its label. Adhesive attachment removes the holes altogether, which is why so much low slope work has moved away from mechanical fastening. The label number and the installed number stop matching.

This is a two component polyurethane that leaves the gun as a low rise foam bead. The beads are run at 12 in on centre, the board is set into them, and the foam rises and cures gripping both faces. It also secures fleece back single ply membrane directly, and it will take multiple layers of insulation, which is the case that makes mechanical attachment awkward. Nothing is drilled, so nothing crosses the thermal layer at all.

The large kit is two canisters at about 92 lb together, with a 25 ft hose, a gun, four mixing tips and three seventeen inch extenders in the box. It needs no compressor, no generator and no pump, which on a roof with no power is the whole argument. Coverage is up to 35 squares for insulation, 3,500 sq ft, or up to 24 squares under fleece back membrane. Everything the kit needs to work arrives inside the two boxes it comes in.

Timing is short and worth knowing before the first bead. Tack time is one to five minutes at around 70°F and set up runs ten to fifteen, so boards are placed as the beads go down rather than after. Ambient and substrate must be 40°F to 100°F, the canisters themselves 70°F to 90°F, and VOC is 25 g/L. Shelf life is sixteen months unopened. The window is short enough that the beads and the boards have to move together across the deck.

matrix-101.title: Matrix 101 SBS Membrane Adhesive
matrix-101.description: Cold applied SBS membrane adhesive superseding hot mopped asphalt, distributing between one and two gallons across every hundred square feet.
about: Cold adhesive exists because of the kettle. Hot mopping means a tank of asphalt at around 450°F somewhere on or beside the building, a crew handling it, fumes coming off it all day and a fire risk that follows the job from the street to the parapet. A cold adhesive puts the same membrane down out of a pail, and everything that goes with the kettle simply stops being part of the job. The kettle disappears from the risk assessment too.

This is the premium of the two GAF cold adhesives and it is a field membrane adhesive: it is used for the field sheet, for base flashings, and at any slope above 1.5 in 12, including at cant transitions. It is glossy black and semi mastic, at over 80% solids, so it sits where it is put on a slope instead of running the way a thinner adhesive does. Body is what keeps an adhesive on a slope rather than at the bottom of it later.

It goes down at 1.5 to 2 gal per 100 sq ft with a sprayer or a notched squeegee, over primed structural concrete, polyiso, an SBS modified sheet or another accepted substrate. The rate moves with how porous that substrate is, which is why the figure is a band rather than a number. A pail holds 4.75 gallons net and weighs 9.5 to 10 lb per gallon. A porous deck drinks adhesive, and the rate has to follow the deck rather than the sheet.

The limits matter as much as the rate. Apply at 45°F and rising and never onto a substrate above 140°F. Do not thin it, do not heat the container, and do not let it freeze. It is not for APP modified membranes, for any sheet with a plastic film or metal foil surface, or over polystyrene, and it is combustible with a flash point above 105°F. Every one of those limits exists because somebody has already had exactly that failure.

matrix-102.title: Matrix 102 SBS Membrane Adhesive
matrix-102.description: Fiber reinforced rubberized cold adhesive for modified bitumen systems, bonding base, interply and cap sheets without any hot asphalt whatsoever.
about: The difference between this and the 101 is the fiber in it. Matrix 102 is a fiber reinforced rubberized adhesive, which gives it body: it bridges a small irregularity in the substrate rather than running off it, and it holds a wet film thickness on a surface that is not perfectly flat. That is exactly the condition a recover job over an existing smooth asphalt roof presents. A recover job is never flat, whatever the survey happened to say about it.

It is asbestos free, and it is built for the whole modified bitumen stack rather than one layer of it. The same pail bonds SBS base sheets, interply sheets and cap sheets, an existing smooth asphalt roof, and Type G2 asphalt coated glass base sheet. GAF call the formulation SURE GRIP and the property they claim for it is flexibility as much as grab. One pail through the whole stack means one product to order and one to store.

Flexibility is the point on a modified bitumen roof, because the system moves. A cap sheet expands and contracts across a day, and an adhesive that cures rigid transfers that movement into the sheet instead of absorbing it. This one is specified to keep its low temperature flexibility, which is the condition where a rigid adhesive gives up first. Rigid is exactly the wrong property for a roof surface that moves every single day.

It goes down at 1.5 to 2 gal per 100 sq ft by sprayer, brush or notched squeegee, at a minimum of 45°F and rising, never onto a substrate above 140°F. gaf-everguard-1121.description: General purpose solvent based contact adhesive for TPO membranes and flashings, covering approximately fifty to seventy square feet per gallon.
about: This is the general purpose adhesive of the EverGuard range and the one most crews still reach for, because the properties that make it unfashionable are the same ones that make it predictable. It is solvent based and fast drying, it has high initial tack, and it behaves the same way on the second day of a job as it did on the first. Predictable is worth a great deal more on a roof than fashionable has ever been, and this one is predictable.

Being a contact adhesive it goes on both the substrate and the back of the membrane, and both faces are left until the solvent has flashed off. Coverage is 50 to 70 sq ft per gallon of bonded membrane, which is roughly half what a water based adhesive gives, so a pail covers less roof and the material cost per square is simply higher. That is the arithmetic worth doing before the order goes in, rather than after it arrives.

What is bought for that is speed and grip. Drying time is fifteen to thirty minutes rather than a wait for water to leave an emulsion, and the initial tack means the sheet stays where it is put on a slope or a parapet instead of creeping while the crew moves on. It is approved over polyisocyanurate insulation and gypsum based cover boards. A sheet that creeps while the crew moves on is a sheet that somebody has to relay later.

tac-203-premium-spray.title: TAC 203 Sprayable Contact Adhesive
tac-203-premium-spray.description: Sprayable polychloroprene contact adhesive with high heat resistance, covering six to eight square metres per litre across most rigid substrates.
about: This is the only adhesive in the range that is not a roofing product, and it earns its place through the work that surrounds a roof rather than the roof itself. Soffit linings, a laminate face on a parapet capping, foam board into a fabricated panel, a vinyl or carpet finish in a plant room: none of it is roofing, and all of it turns up on the same invoice. The work that surrounds a roof is still work that somebody has to price.

The base is polychloroprene, which is what gives it the heat resistance the grade is sold on. A contact adhesive under a dark laminate or against a metal face in a roof space is working at temperatures a general purpose adhesive will soften at, and a bond that creeps in summer and holds in winter is not a bond that anybody wants in a finished job. Creep is the failure that shows up in August rather than on the day it was fitted.

It is a contact adhesive in the strict sense, so both faces are sprayed, both are left until the film is no longer tacky to the touch, and the two are then joined and pressed hard. There is no second chance once they meet. Evaporation takes five to ten minutes at 20°C and the open time is ten to fifteen, which sets how large a piece one person can handle. The size of the piece is set by the open time, not by the man lifting it.

Coverage is 6 to 8 m² per litre, and the working conditions are specific: 20°C for materials and adhesive, timber at 8 to 10% moisture and 60 to 70% relative humidity. Do not use it below 10°C, because condensation forms on the film and the bond simply fails. It cleans up with TAC 101 and has a twelve month shelf life stored out of the sun. Below ten degrees the film collects water and the bond is lost before it ever starts.

dupont-tyvek-120.title: Tyvek Protec 120 Underlayment
dupont-tyvek-120.description: High traction synthetic underlayment that shields the deck from moisture with confident walkability, covering one thousand square feet per roll.
about: DuPont Tyvek Protec 120 is a four layer synthetic roofing underlayment built on an embossed non woven technology. Grooves in the top layer carry dirt and water off the surface, a lamination layer acts as the water barrier, a woven polypropylene scrim adds strength, and a slip resistant coating grips the deck. It stays walkable dry, wet, hot, cold or dirty, lays flat and holds chalk marks. It belongs to a portfolio that also includes Protec 160 and 200.

The standard roll is 48 in by 250 ft, ten squares or 1,000 sq ft, and a two square roll of 48 in by 50 ft is also offered. Nominal thickness is 0.248 mm, 9.76 mils, at about 25 lb per roll. gcp-5003000.title: Grace Ultra Butyl Underlayment

It is the right choice wherever the membrane has to hold high service temperatures for long stretches: the desert southwest, alpine roofs, and under copper, zinc or Cor-Ten panels that conduct heat straight into the underlayment. gaf-everguard-wb181.title: EverGuard WB181 Bonding Adhesive
gaf-everguard-wb181.description: Water based acrylic emulsion bonding adhesive for TPO and PVC roofing membranes, covering approximately six hundred square feet per container.
about: The reason this adhesive is water based has very little to do with the roof and a great deal to do with the building underneath it. A solvent bonding adhesive puts its smell through every vent, stairwell and open window for as long as the crew is working, and on an occupied building that is the thing that generates the complaints. At under 20 g/L of VOC this one is close to odourless. Odour is what gets a crew asked to stop work.

It is an acrylic emulsion copolymer, and it bonds both smooth and fleece back TPO as well as fleece back PVC. The substrate list is the useful part: polyiso and fiber board, insulations, fiberglass faced gypsum panels, and for flashings concrete, masonry, metal and wood. That covers most of what a commercial deck actually presents once the old roof is off and the boards are down. That list is most of what a commercial deck actually is.

The two membrane types are applied in opposite ways and getting them the wrong way round ruins the bond. Smooth reinforced membrane takes adhesive on both the substrate and the underside of the sheet, and the membrane goes down only once the adhesive has dried clear. Fleece back takes adhesive on the substrate alone and the sheet goes into it wet, before it dries. Dry for smooth sheet, wet for fleece back, and never the other way round.

Coverage runs 115 to 125 sq ft per gallon on smooth membrane, about 600 sq ft of bonded area per pail. Weight is 8.6 to 9 lb per gallon, solids 60 to 65%, viscosity 14,000 to 18,000 cps. Minimum application temperature is 40°F and rising, and the pail must be stored above 40°F because a frozen emulsion is a ruined emulsion and there is no way back from it. A pail that has frozen once is a pail to send back, not to stir harder.

gaf-778c.title: EverGuard PVC Quick Lay Adhesive
gaf-778c.description: Single sided water based adhesive for smooth PVC membrane, installed directly into wet film for approximately fifty percent faster application.
about: Every contact adhesive on a roof costs the same two things: a second coat and a wait. The sheet is coated, the deck is coated, and then nobody touches anything until both have flashed off. That waiting is dead time on a large deck, and it is the reason a crew of five finishes fewer squares in a day than the arithmetic of the job would suggest they should. The arithmetic looks fine on paper and the working day never quite matches it.

This one removes both costs. It goes on the substrate only, and the membrane is rolled into it while it is still wet rather than after it has dried. GAF put the gain at close to fifty percent against a traditional solvent bonding adhesive, which in practice is the difference between finishing a section before the afternoon and coming back for it tomorrow. Half a day saved on a large deck becomes a full day across the whole job.

The trade is that the wet window is now the thing you have to manage. Dried adhesive is a failed bond here, not a ready one, so the adhesive goes down at the rate the crew can actually follow, and the sheet is broomed while the film is still open. Applied at 100 sq ft per gallon that is roughly 600 sq ft, six squares, of installed membrane from one pail. The pail no longer sets the pace of the work; the crew behind it does.

titebond-61001.title: WeatherMaster Metal Roof Sealant
titebond-61001.description: Advanced polymer metal roofing sealant rated at fifty percent joint movement, applied from zero degrees Fahrenheit onto still damp surfaces.
about: A metal roof is a structure that never stops moving. A long panel grows and shrinks with every sunrise and every night, and the joint at its end has to absorb that for twenty years without splitting. This sealant carries a joint movement rating of plus or minus fifty percent of the joint width, which is the number that decides whether a seal survives a decade of that or fails in its third summer. Most sealant failures are movement failures.

It is an advanced polymer rather than a silicone or a urethane, and that choice drives most of what makes it usable. It bonds to Kynar coated metal, to aluminium, galvanised steel, copper and to most standard building materials, and it takes paint an hour after it goes on. A silicone does neither of those things, which is why silicone on a painted panel is a repair waiting to happen. That is why the choice of chemistry is not a detail.

The two figures that matter on site are the ones nobody reads until it is cold or wet. Air, sealant and surface temperature have to be above 0°F, which puts the tool in the winter bag rather than the summer one, and unlike most sealants it will bond to wet and damp surfaces. Neither of those is a convenience; they are what let a leak be closed on the day it is found. A leak found on a wet afternoon can be closed on that afternoon.

The cartridge is 10.1 oz, which lays about 53 linear feet at a 3/16 in bead. It is 99% solids, so it does not shrink back into the joint as it cures, at 9 g/L of VOC. Tack free comes at 20 to 30 minutes and full cure at 24 hours. It meets ASTM C920 Type S, Grade NS, Class 50. It is not made for continuous submersion or any use below the waterline. Ninety nine percent solids is what stops a bead sinking into the joint as it cures.

dewalt-dcs391.title: Cordless Circular Sidewinder Saw
dewalt-dcs391.description: Sidewinder configuration circular saw combining lightweight magnesium construction with a carbide tipped blade measuring six and a half inches across.
about: This is the sidewinder layout, which means the motor sits in line with the blade rather than behind a gearbox at right angles to it. That makes the tool shorter front to back and lighter in the hand than a worm drive, and on a roof, where you are usually cutting sheathing on your knees or trimming panel on a pair of trestles, shorter and lighter is what actually matters over a full day of work. A worm drive earns its keep framing, not up here.

DeWalt's own manual puts the no load speed at 5,150 rpm and the maximum depth of cut at 55 mm, which is the 2 1/8 in the US listings quote at 90 degrees and 1 5/8 in once the shoe is tipped over to 45. The blade is 6 1/2 in on a 5/8 in arbor and the bevel travels from zero through to 50 degrees. Bare weight without a battery is 2.9 kg, near enough 6.4 lb. Those are the figures from the manufacturer rather than from a retailer listing.

The shoe is magnesium rather than pressed steel, and that is the part of a circular saw that decides whether your cuts stay true after the tool has been dropped off a staging plank a few times. Magnesium keeps its flatness and shrugs off the knocks that would put a permanent twist in a stamped shoe, and it is lighter, which is where a good part of the weight saving comes from. A twisted shoe is a saw that never cuts straight again.

It runs on the same 20V MAX battery as the rest of the DeWalt cordless line, so on a site already carrying that platform there is nothing extra to charge or carry. A carbide tipped blade ships in the box and nothing else, since this is sold as a bare tool. DeWalt covers it with a three year limited warranty, one year of free service and ninety days of satisfaction guarantee. Batteries and the charger are bought separately.

dewalt-dwht51002.title: Sixteen Ounce Steel Nailing Hammer
dewalt-dwht51002.description: Sixteen ounce nailing hammer manufactured from a single continuous forging of steel, incorporating magnetic nail start and side puller slot.
about: A hammer made from one piece of steel has no joint between the head and the handle, which is the place where a wooden or fiberglass hammer eventually gives up. Nothing works loose because there is nothing to work loose, and the whole shaft is heat treated rather than just the striking face. On a roof that means the tool survives being thrown into a bucket at the end of every day. A wooden handle would have split long before then.

The trade against that is vibration, because steel transmits the shock of a missed nail straight into the wrist in a way a wooden handle never does. DeWalt answer that with an anti slip grip moulded over the shaft, which takes the worst of the sting and, more usefully on a steep pitch, keeps the handle in a wet glove. The claimed balance point is set to smooth the swing. A steel hammer is a trade off and not a free upgrade.

It is a 16 oz head on an 11 3/4 in handle, which is the general carpentry size rather than a framing weight. The face is smooth and shield shaped, so it leaves no waffle mark on anything that will be seen, and the claw is curved for pulling rather than ripped straight for demolition. That combination is aimed at finish work and cabinet work as much as at a roof. A framing weight would only tire the wrist out on work like this.

Two details save time. A magnetic nail start holds a nail on the face so it can be set one handed, which matters when the other hand is holding a ladder or a course of starter strip. dewalt-dcm849.title: Brushless Cordless Rotary Polisher
dewalt-dcm849.description: Brushless cordless rotary polisher carrying a seven inch backing plate, variable continuously between eight hundred and twenty two hundred revolutions.
about: On a metal roof the polisher is a finishing tool rather than a cleaning one. Standing seam and stone coated panels arrive with a factory finish that no site process improves, but coping, flashing and fabricated trim get cut, handled and scratched, and a rotary with the right pad is how those marks are taken back before the piece goes up where everyone can see it. Nobody polishes a factory finish; they polish what the site did to it.

The pad is 7 in on a 5/8 in by 11 spindle, which is the common thread across backing plates and compounds, so pads are not tied to this tool. Speed runs from 800 to 2,200 rpm and it is variable two ways: on the trigger for feathering into a start, and on a dial for setting a ceiling so the trigger cannot run away with a compound that burns at speed. That independence from the tool itself is worth a good deal more than it sounds.

Low speed is what most of this work needs. A polisher held at full speed on a painted panel will burn the coating through before it ever polishes it, and the dial is what stops an unfamiliar hand from doing that. The rubber overmold on the gear case is there for grip, and it also takes the edge off the marks the tool leaves when it is set down on finished metal. Burned paint on a visible trim piece is a piece you end up buying twice.

It can be held by the front grip or by a side handle, so the same tool works flat on a bench and up on edge against a length of coping. dewalt-dcn681.title: Cordless Brushless Stapler 18 Gauge
dewalt-dcn681.description: Brushless cordless stapler driving eighteen gauge narrow crown staples, with selectable sequential or contact actuation and tool free depth adjustment.
about: Synthetic underlayment goes down faster with a stapler than with cap nails, and on a deck that is already dry a narrow crown staple holds the sheet flat without the head of a cap fastener standing proud under the shingle above it. This is the cordless version of that job, so there is no compressor idling on the drive and no hose snaking up the ladder behind you all morning. Nothing sits idling on the drive while you work.

It drives 18 gauge staples with a 1/4 in narrow crown, in leg lengths from 1/2 in up to 1 1/2 in, and the magazine holds 100 of them. The motor is brushless, which on a fastening tool matters less for runtime than for the consistency of the drive: the last staple in a magazine sets to the same depth as the first, rather than tailing off as the battery sags toward the end of its charge. That consistency is the real argument for brushless here.

Two of the controls are worth knowing before the tool leaves the van. The trigger is selectable without any tool between sequential mode, where you place the nose then pull, and contact mode, where you hold the trigger and bump along a run. Depth is also adjusted by hand, so a staple can be set flush on soft sheathing and driven harder into something dense. Both settings change without opening a case or hunting for a key.

tolsen-25012.title: Fiberglass Handle Stoning Hammer
tolsen-25012.description: Professional stoning hammer combining a 1,500 gram drop forged head with a fiberglass reinforced handle, totalling 1.68 kilograms once assembled.
about: A stoning hammer is not a framing hammer with a different name. It has no claw and it is not meant to drive nails; it is a mass on a stick, used to dress stone, to seat a concrete tile onto its batten and to break the piece that has to come off before the new one goes on. On a tiled or slated roof that is a daily job, and a claw hammer does it badly and marks everything it touches. The right tool for stone has always been a blunt one.

The head weighs 1,500 g and the whole tool 1.68 kg, so roughly nine tenths of what you are swinging is head. That ratio is the point of the design: the energy goes into the stone rather than into the arm that moved it, and a lighter handle lets the same worker keep swinging for longer. Overall the tool measures 295 by 45 by 110 mm, which is short enough to work close in against a wall. Nine tenths in the head is what a dressing hammer is for.

The head is drop forged from special tool steel and then heat treated, which is what stops it mushrooming over its own edges after a season of hitting masonry. Forging aligns the grain of the steel around the shape instead of cutting through it, and that is the difference between a head that wears and a head that cracks. The black paint is there to keep rust off it between jobs. A cracked head is the one failure that cannot be filed out.

The handle is fiberglass rather than wood, so it does not swell in the wet, dry out in a truck or split at the eye the way an ash handle eventually will. Tolsen publish no grip specification, no striking face dimension, no warranty term and no conformity standard for this hammer, so none of the four is claimed here, and Roofpro cover the hammer for a year instead. Wood is still the traditional choice, and it is still the part that fails first.

tolsen-10243.title: Eighteen Inch Bolt Cutter
tolsen-10243.description: Eighteen inch compound bolt cutter carrying drop forged hardened jaws, adjustable and replaceable, between tubular steel handles with cushioned grips.
about: Roofing generates more things that need cutting off than most trades admit. Anchor straps, banding round a pallet of tile, the padlock nobody has a key for, threaded rod left long through a purlin, snow guard wire, the odd bit of rebar in a parapet. A saw does all of it eventually and a grinder does it with sparks on a roof, which is the one thing nobody wants near felt. A cutter is the tool that does all of it cold and quietly.

This cutter is 450 mm long, which is the short end of the range and deliberately so. Full length bolt cutters are four feet of leverage that will not fit in a bag, will not swing in a loft and cannot be worked one handed on a ladder. Eighteen inches goes in the van, gets carried up, and still cuts what a roof actually presents rather than what a demolition site does. A tool that stays in the van is a tool that cuts nothing at all.

The leverage comes from a compound linkage instead of raw handle length. Two pivots in series multiply the hand force twice over, so a short tool closes jaws that a single pivot of the same size could never move. It is the same trick a compound lopper uses on green wood, and it is why the length of the handles stops being the only thing that decides what will cut. Leverage bought with geometry costs nothing in length or in weight.

The jaws are drop forged from high carbon steel, hardened, polished, and both adjustable and replaceable, so the pair can be reset as they wear rather than the tool being thrown out with them. The handles are tubular steel with cushioned non slip grips. Tolsen publish no cutting capacity and no weight for it, and no warranty either, so Roofpro cover it for a year. A pair of jaws that can be reset is what gives the tool a second life.

supatool-20in.title: Hardened Blade Carpentry Handsaw
supatool-20in.description: Professional twenty inch carpentry handsaw carrying hardened heat treated universal teeth at seven points per inch, cutting in both directions.
about: There is a stubborn assumption that a circular saw has retired the handsaw, and anyone who has cut one sheet of decking in the rain knows better. A handsaw needs no battery, no cord and no guard check, it starts the moment it touches the wood, and it is the only saw that can be worked lying across a rafter bay with one arm through the framing to reach the cut. It is also the only one that never runs out of charge halfway up a slope.

The blade is 500 mm, twenty inches, at seven points to the inch. That tooth count is the compromise the whole tool is built around: coarse enough that it clears sawdust and moves through a deck board without binding, fine enough that it leaves an edge worth nailing to rather than the torn exit a four point rip saw gives on plywood and thin sheathing. Seven points is the count most site carpentry settles on, and for good reason.

The teeth are hardened and the blade heat treated, which is the modern trade off. A hardened tooth holds an edge far longer than an untreated one and survives the grit, nails and old felt that a roof puts in front of it, but it is too hard to be reset with a file, so the saw is used until it is done and then replaced rather than being sharpened. It is a saw that gets used up rather than maintained, and for the price that is a fair trade.

The tooth pattern is universal, meaning it cuts on the push and on the pull rather than only on one stroke. On a bench that is a convenience; overhead, working into a bay or under a low rafter where the return stroke is all the room there is, it is the difference between cutting and not. Supatool publish no blade material, handle material or weight for it. Neither figure changes how the saw cuts, but neither is invented here either.

qualcraft-2560p.title: Shingle Tear Off Demolition Shovel
qualcraft-2560p.description: Fifty four inch shingle demolition shovel incorporating a heat tempered steel head, ten working teeth and ergonomically offset steel handle.
about: Tearing a roof off is the part of the job nobody photographs, and it is also the part that decides how the day goes. A flat spade lifts shingles and leaves every nail behind; a proper tear off shovel lifts the shingle and the nail together in one movement, and the difference across a whole roof is measured in hours rather than in minutes of saved effort. The tool pays for itself on the very first roof that you strip with it.

The head is all steel, 9 3/4 x 10 1/2 in, with ten teeth along the working edge and that edge heat tempered so it keeps its bite through nails and grit instead of rolling over after the first slope. Those teeth are what straddle a nail head and let the shaft do the pulling, and the head will draw nails up to 16D, which covers anything holding a shingle down. An edge that has rolled over is a shovel that has stopped working.

The handle is the part that is easy to overlook. It is steel rather than wood or fiberglass, 22 1/2 in of it, and it is offset rather than straight. That offset is what puts the fulcrum under the load so the lift comes from the shovel and not from your back, and it is the reason a tear off shovel is worth carrying separately from an ordinary spade. A straight handle puts that same load straight through your lower back instead.

Overall the tool measures 54 in, which is long enough to work standing upright on a shallow pitch. A vinyl grip covers the top of the shaft. Qualcraft build it for fiberglass and asphalt shingle work specifically. No weight figure and no warranty term are published for the tool, so that one is left unstated, while Guardian warrant the tool for its lifetime. Anything else published about it comes from a retailer rather than from Qualcraft itself.

dewalt-dcpr320.title: Cordless Battery Powered Pruner
dewalt-dcpr320.description: Cordless pruning shears engineered to sever branches approaching one and a half inches, delivering approximately eleven hundred cuts per charge.
about: The reason a pruner belongs in a roofing catalogue has nothing to do with gardening. Branches that overhang a roof drop leaves into the valleys, hold moisture against the shingles and give squirrels a bridge onto the deck, and the cure is cutting them back rather than cleaning the roof twice a year forever. This is the tool that does that from a ladder with one hand free. A branch left where it is will put the same leaves back down next autumn.

It severs stems and shrubs up to 1 1/2 in, and DeWalt quote around 1,100 cuts from a single charge, which is far more than a day of trimming back around a house will ever ask of it. The tool weighs 3 lb bare. DeWalt also claim it takes roughly sixteen times less effort on average than a manual pruner, which is the point when a hundred cuts are in front of you. Three pounds is light enough to hold out at arm reach for a while.

The blades carry a non stick coating, which matters more than it sounds on green wood, because sap is what gums a pruner until the cut stops being clean and starts crushing the stem instead. A blade change tool ships with it, so a dulled blade is replaced on the job rather than sharpened badly or left to tear through everything for the rest of the week. Sap is what turns a clean cut into a crushed one over a single afternoon.

An onboard LED lights the cut, which sounds like a gimmick until you are reaching into the shaded side of a hedge against a wall. It runs on the same 20V MAX battery as the rest of the DeWalt line and comes as a bare tool. Motor type, blade speed and any cutting standard are not published for it, so none of the three is stated here. Batteries and a charger are bought separately, as with every bare tool in the DeWalt cordless line.

dewalt-dwht36225.title: Twenty Five Foot Measuring Tape
dewalt-dwht36225.description: Twenty five foot tape measure delivering thirteen feet of unsupported standout, inside impact resistant housing withstanding a sixty foot drop.
about: Standout is the figure that matters on a roof and it is the one most people never look at. It is how far the blade will reach out unsupported before it folds, and at 13 ft this tape will cross a rafter bay, run up a slope or reach the far side of a chimney without a second person holding the end. On the ground that is convenience; on a pitch it is safety. Most tapes give up somewhere around eight or nine feet of unsupported reach.

The blade is 25 ft long and 1 1/4 in wide in high carbon steel, coated in yellow thermoplastic. The last 9 in carry a heavier coat, because the end of a blade is where the wear happens: it is dragged over shingles, snapped back a hundred times a day and bent around the hook. That heavier section is what postpones the break that eventually retires every tape. That section is what decides how long the whole tape lasts in a bag.

Inside the case is Dual Core, a patented arrangement of two retracting springs instead of one. Two smaller springs fit a shorter case than one long one, which is why a tape of this reach is not the brick it would otherwise be, and it also spreads the work so neither spring is doing the whole job every time the blade goes back in. It is also the reason the case is shorter than a tape of this reach would otherwise need to be.

The case is an impact resistant blend of polycarbonate and ABS that DeWalt rate for a 60 ft drop, which is the number that speaks to where this tape is expected to be used. The hook connection is reinforced against the tearing that kills a blade at the rivets. DeWalt cover their hand tools with a limited lifetime warranty. Sixty feet describes a roof rather than a workshop bench, which tells you where DeWalt expect this tape to spend its life.

dewalt-dccs620.title: Compact Cordless Brushless Chainsaw
dewalt-dccs620.description: Compact brushless chainsaw carrying a twelve inch Oregon guide bar, with automatic chain oiling and completely tool free tensioning adjustment.
about: A chainsaw is not a roofing tool until the day a limb comes down across the ridge, or until the tree that has been dropping needles into the valley for ten years finally has to be cut back from the eaves. That is the job this size is built for: short cuts, awkward angles, and nothing like the felling work that would justify carrying a petrol saw up a ladder. Nobody buys this saw to fell a tree, and that is the point of it.

The bar is 12 in of Oregon, running a chain of 3/8 in pitch on a 0.043 in gauge at 25.2 feet per second. It is a low kickback chain, which on a saw that will be used occasionally rather than daily is the right choice, because kickback is what catches out the operator who has not held a saw in six months. Bare weight is 7.8 lb, about 9 lb once a battery is on it. An occasional user is exactly who a low kickback chain protects.

Two of the conveniences are worth the money on an occasional tool. Tensioning is tool free, so the chain is adjusted by hand with a knob rather than by hunting for a scrench that went missing two jobs ago. Oiling is automatic, which removes the other classic failure of the occasional user, running a dry chain until the bar is blued and the chain is ruined. Both of those failures end up costing a good deal more than the saw itself.

The motor is brushless, which matters more for a battery tool than for a corded one because every watt not lost to brush friction is runtime you did not have to charge. It runs on the same 20V MAX battery as the rest of the DeWalt line and ships bare. DeWalt covers it with a three year limited warranty on the same terms as their other cordless tools. Batteries and a charger are bought separately, as with every bare tool.

hxoutdoors-ft16c.title: Full Tang Tactical Camping Hatchet
hxoutdoors-ft16c.description: Full tang tactical camping hatchet stretching twelve point eight inches overall, forged from 420 stainless hardened to fifty eight Rockwell.
about: A hatchet earns its place on a roof through the three jobs at the back of it rather than the one at the front. It splits a batten to length, it drives a stake into sheathing for a rope, it pulls the nail nobody can reach with a bar, and it breaks apart what the tear off shovel has already lifted. The chopping edge is almost the least of what it does across a working day. Most of that is work that a shovel or a pry bar does badly.

It runs 12.83 in overall on a 3.74 in edge, which is short for an axe and long for a knife, and that is the span where a tool can still be swung one handed from a ladder. Bare it weighs 711 g. Anything heavier stops being a tool you carry up and becomes one you fetch, and a tool that has to be fetched is a tool that sits in the van all day. Weight is the quiet reason good tools stay in the van, and this one is under two pounds of it.

The steel is 420 hardened to 58 HRC, which is harder than a general purpose stainless and a deliberate choice for an edge that meets nails, grit and old shingle rather than clean wood. The blade is full tang, so the steel runs unbroken from edge to pommel and the handle scales are bolted to it. A hidden tang is where a hatchet breaks, and this one has no hidden tang to break. Hidden tangs are why cheap hatchets fail at the handle.

The scales are G10 composite in a blackened stone wash, which does not swell, rot or lose grip when wet, and the poll is finished as a hammer face with a pry bar and nail slot cut into the tail. It ships in a Kydex sheath with a belt clip. HX Outdoors publish no warranty term for it, so the cover in the table is Roofpro's own year rather than theirs. dewalt-dwht10998.title: Retractable Blade Cutting Knife
dewalt-dwht10998.description: Retractable utility knife storing five replacement blades internally, with three positive slider stops governing exactly how much edge stays exposed.
about: A utility knife is the tool a roofer picks up more often than anything else, and it is also the one most often found with a dull blade still in it. Shingle granules blunt an edge in minutes, synthetic underlayment blunts it faster, and a blunt blade tears where it ought to slice. The cure was never a better blade; it is having the next one already inside the handle instead of in a box on the truck. That is the whole argument for this one.

This knife carries five replacement blades in the body, which sounds trivial until you count the trips back down a ladder that it saves across a week of work. The change is made without a tool, so it happens where the cutting is rather than at the tailgate, and a blade that swaps in ten seconds gets swapped the moment it dulls rather than being pushed through another two squares of roof. Five blades is the better part of a working week.

The slider has three positive stops, so the exposed edge is set to the material in front of it rather than left wherever it happened to land. A short setting scores a shingle without ever reaching the underlayment beneath it, while the full setting cuts felt and wrap in a single pass. The blade lock holds that setting under load, which is what stops an edge creeping back mid cut. A cut that wanders into the felt below is a repair, not a cut.

The body is zinc, which is why it survives the drop off a roof and the boot that lands on it afterwards, and it takes the standard utility blade that every supplier on the job already stocks by the hundred. DeWalt cover their hand tools with a limited lifetime warranty. Bare weight, closed length and the contents of the carton are not published, so none of the three is stated here. None of those three figures changes how the knife is used.

dewalt-dxl2010.title: Four Foot Aluminum Stepladder Type IA
dewalt-dxl2010.description: Four foot aluminum stepladder rated Type IA for three hundred pounds, incorporating gusseted bracing, pail shelf and slip resistant footings.
about: Duty rating is the only number on a ladder that matters, and it is the one people read last. Type IA means 300 lb, and that figure is not the worker: it is the worker, the boots, the belt, the tools in it and whatever is being carried up. A hundred and eighty pound roofer with a bundle on one shoulder is already most of the way there, which is why a lighter rating is a false economy. The rating covers everything that leaves the ground with you.

At four feet this is a working height ladder rather than an access one. It is what gets a soffit, a gutter return, a low eave, a garage rake or a chimney flashing within reach without dragging an extension around the house. Four feet also fits in a van without folding seats down, which decides more often than anyone admits which ladder actually arrives at the job. The ladder that actually arrives at the house is the one that does the work.

The rails are aluminum with gusset bracing, which is the detail that keeps a stepladder from racking sideways as it ages. A ladder that flexes when you shift weight is not yet unsafe, but it is on the way, and bracing is what postpones that. The feet are slip resistant, and the step surface is a quarter larger than the standard, which is felt over a full day. Bracing is most of what you are paying for when two ladders look identical.

The top is set up to work from rather than stand on: a magnet holds fasteners and the slots take a driver or a bar, so neither goes in a pocket nor off the edge. There is a pail shelf below it. The ladder meets both ANSI and OSHA requirements. DeWalt publish no weight for this model, and their three year term excludes it, so Roofpro cover it a year. Neither absence changes how the ladder is used, and neither is guessed at here.

masterplug-cma301116g4sl.title: Thirty Foot Cable Cassette Reel
masterplug-cma301116g4sl.description: Thirty foot cassette reel carrying sixteen gauge cable to four shuttered grounded outlets, protected by an integrated thermal overload cutout.
about: The failure that puts a cable reel in a roofing catalogue is not electrical. It is thirty feet of cord lying across a roof, over a ladder rung, round a bundle and through the one place someone has to walk. A reel is how that same thirty feet leaves the ground as a wound drum, pays out only what the job needs, and goes back the same way at the end of the day. A cord across the ground is a trip hazard, and a cord across a roof is worse.

This one is a cassette rather than a drum on a frame, so it lies flat, hangs on a hook and takes up a fraction of the room in a van. There is a winding handle for the recovery, which sounds obvious until you have wound thirty feet in by hand. The cord is high visibility, which is the cheapest safety feature ever invented and the one most often left out. Space in a van is the constraint that nobody ever writes into a specification.

The cable is 16 AWG rated at 10 A across four grounded outlets, all of them shuttered. Shutters matter more outdoors than in: an open socket on a roof collects grit, rain and roofing granules, and the shutter is what keeps all three out of the contacts. A power switch cuts the whole reel at once rather than leaving four live outlets in the weather. Contacts that stay clean are the contacts still working at the end of a winter.

A thermal overload cutout sits in the reel itself, which is the part that matters with a wound cable. Cord left coiled on a drum cannot shed heat the way a run out cable can, so a load that is safe unwound is not always safe wound, and the cutout is what covers that. A power indicator shows the reel is live. Masterplug warrant it for three years. Three years is a long warranty on a thing that gets dragged around for a living.

dewalt-dpg737.title: Two Layer Thermal Insulated Gloves
dewalt-dpg737.description: Insulated roofing gloves constructed glove inside glove, combining a fifteen gauge nylon outer shell over seven gauge acrylic thermal insulation.
about: Cold is not the reason a roofer loses a day; a cold hand is. Grip goes first, then the fine movement needed to start a nail or hold a blade square, and what follows is either slower work or a mistake. The usual answer is a thick glove, which solves the cold by removing the feel, and a roof is the one place where feel is what keeps hands on the material and off the edge. Warmth that costs you the feel of the work is not warmth worth having.

The design here is two gloves rather than one. A 15 gauge nylon shell takes the abrasion and holds the shape of a hand, and inside it a 7 gauge acrylic liner does the insulating. Separating those two jobs is what lets each be thin: the shell stays close enough to feel a fastener through, and the warmth is carried by a layer that never has to be tough. Thin and warm are only opposites for as long as both jobs live in one layer.

The palm is dipped three quarters of the way up in micro foam, which is the part that does the gripping. Foam dip works wet as well as dry, because the texture opens rather than closing into a smooth film the way a solid coating does, and roofing is a wet trade for a good part of the year. The undipped back is what lets the glove breathe instead of soaking. A glove that grips only when dry is a glove for a different trade entirely.

The dip stopping short of the cuff is deliberate: a fully coated glove is warmer and does not vent, and a hand sweating inside a sealed glove gets cold faster than one that never sweated at all. DeWalt publish no sizing table, no standard, no weight and no warranty term for this glove, so none of those is stated here, and the cover shown is Roofpro's own year. A vented back is worth more over a full day than another layer of lining.

Keep the dipped palm to the work and the bare back to the weather
Let them dry fully between days rather than starting damp and cold

Treat them as warmth and grip, not as cut protection, which they are not

palmer-v5501.title: Roofer Fall Arrest Protection Kit
palmer-v5501.description: Comprehensive roofer fall arrest kit combining a five point harness, fifty foot vertical lifeline, rope grab and reusable structural anchorage.
about: A fall arrest kit is bought as one item because it only works as one. A harness with the wrong lanyard, an anchor rated for something else or a rope grab that does not match the line are each a system that has not been tested as a system, and the failure never shows up until the one moment the whole thing exists for. This kit ships already matched. A system is only ever tested as the exact set of parts it was certified with.

The harness is five point with a dorsal D ring, which is the attachment that keeps a worker upright after arrest rather than folded. The lifeline is 50 ft of 5/8 in rope carrying a rope grab, and the grab connects through a shock absorbing lanyard. That lanyard is the component that turns a sudden stop into a survivable one by paying out under load. Stopping a fall is easy; stopping one without injury is what is being bought.

Capacity runs from 130 to 310 lb, and both ends of that range are real limits rather than a single maximum. Too light a user does not load an energy absorber enough to deploy it as designed, and too heavy a one overruns the arrest distance the absorber was rated for. Every load bearing fitting in the kit is alloy steel, with three quarter inch snap hooks. A range with a floor surprises people who only ever read the top number.

The anchor is reusable rather than single use, so it comes off at the end of the job instead of being left in the deck, and the whole kit packs into a four gallon bucket that also serves as the thing it lives in. The harness meets ANSI Z359.11 and the anchor ANSI Z359.18. Palmer Safety publish no warranty term, so the kit carries a year of Roofpro cover. An anchor left behind in a finished roof is a leak somebody finds years later.

Check the user weight falls inside the 130 to 310 lb range before use

bilco-s20.title: Type S Roof Access Galvanized Hatch
bilco-s20.description: Single leaf ladder access hatch, fiberglass insulated cover, twelve inch galvannealed curb reinforced throughout for forty pounds per square foot.
about: The Bilco Type S is a single leaf roof hatch made for ladder access, and the design turns on one hand operation: the cover travels to fully open or fully closed without the user ever letting go of the ladder, which is the whole safety argument for specifying it. Units arrive pre assembled from the factory. This one is the S-20, built in galvanized steel; the same hatch exists in aluminum and in stainless. The 30 in dimension is the hinge side.

The cover is 14 gauge galvannealed steel with a 3 in beaded flange and formed reinforcing members, and it carries 1 in of fiberglass insulation behind a protective 22 gauge metal liner. A heavy extruded EPDM gasket is bonded to the inside of the cover, so closing it compresses a continuous seal onto the top of the curb. The curb stands 12 in tall in the same gauge, insulated with 1 in of rigid high density fiberboard on its outside face.

The curb carries an integral metal capflashing in the same gauge and material, fully welded at the corners, with the Bil-Clip system: stamped tabs on 6 in centres that bend inward to hold single ply roofing membrane securely in place. A 3 1/2 in flange with 7/16 in holes fixes the frame to the deck. Compression spring operators inside telescopic tubes carry the cover through the whole arc of travel. The upper tube sits outermost so grit cannot collect.

The cover is reinforced for a minimum 40 psf live load with deflection held to 1/150 of the span, and the design pressure is plus or minus 100 psf with a design factor of 2. The galvanized steel and aluminum versions carry a Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance and Florida Building Code approval. Bilco warrants materials and workmanship for five years. Hardware is zinc plated and chromate sealed, and the steel ships red oxide primed.

duration-designer-slatestone-grey.title: Duration Designer Slatestone Grey
duration-designer-slatestone-grey.description: Architectural shingles incorporating a SureNail fabric strip that reinforces the nailing zone against powerful winds on particularly exposed coastal roofs.
about: Duration Designer (Owens Corning) is an architectural shingle from the TruDefinition Duration series, in Slatestone Grey. Its patented SureNail Technology is the only reinforced nailing zone on the face of a shingle: a woven fabric strip embedded across both layers, giving Triple Layer Protection against nail pull and up to 200% wider bond between the layers than standard shingles. Tru Bond weathering grade asphalt sealant holds each course down.

Each shingle is nominally 13 1/4 x 39 3/8 in with a 5 5/8 in exposure. A square takes 64 shingles in 3 bundles covering 98.4 sq ft. StreakGuard blends copper lined 3M granules against blue green algae; Owens Corning Hip and Ridge shingles match the Designer colors. The deck can be 6 in boards, 3/8 in plywood or 7/16 in OSB. From 4:12 up, Owens Corning synthetic underlayment or one meeting ASTM D8257; from 2:12 to under 4:12, two layers.

Use galvanized steel, stainless steel or aluminum nails with a minimum 12 gauge shank and 3/8 in head, placed inside the SureNail fastening area and driven at least 3/4 in into the wood deck or through it by 1/4 in, preferably meeting ASTM F1667. Slopes over 60 degrees (21 in per foot) require six nails and four spots of asphalt roofing cement per shingle. Store bundles flat in a covered, ventilated area below 110°F, handling them with care below 40°F.

Warranty: Limited Lifetime. Wind coverage reaches up to 160 mph when the Owens Corning component requirements are met and starter shingles are installed on both the eaves and the rakes. The 25 year algae resistance coverage, effective January 1, 2024, requires an approved Owens Corning Hip and Ridge product. about: This is Steeldash snap lock standing seam in 24 gauge steel, finished in Slate Gray. gibraltar-cf5g-26.title: Galvanized Steel Counter Flashing
gibraltar-cf5g-26.description: Galvanized counter flashing protecting the exposed upper edge of chimney step flashing, formed from straight twenty six gauge steel sections.
about: Counter flashing is the piece that finishes a roof to wall joint. Step flashing carries the water out from under the shingles, but its top edge is left open, and this Gibraltar profile covers that edge so nothing can run behind it. The section is 5 in on the face by 1/2 in on the return, formed from 26 gauge galvanized steel and supplied in straight 10 ft lengths. Gibraltar describes the job plainly: it protects the top edge of step flashing.

The short 1/2 in leg is the part that goes into the wall. It sits in a raked out mortar joint or in a reglet cut into masonry, and the joint is sealed once the leg is in. The 5 in face then hangs down over the step flashing below it, so the two pieces overlap without either being fastened through the other, which is what lets the wall and the roof move apart. Nothing is screwed through the face, so neither piece restrains the other.

Gibraltar lists the profile for roof slopes of 3:12 and steeper. On a shallower plane the water moves slowly enough that a lapped counter flashing is no longer the right detail, and a soldered or fully adhered flashing takes over. Lengths lap each other by about 4 in, always arranged so the upper piece sits over the lower one and the lap sheds water. On a steeper plane the same lap sheds faster and the detail gets easier, not harder.

The steel is mill galvanized, with a zinc coating that holds off corrosion and takes paint if the wall colour matters. It is a companion piece rather than a substitute: the step flashing underneath still does the work of moving water out of the joint, and the sealant at the reglet still has to be inspected as part of normal roof maintenance. A failed bead at the reglet is the usual way this detail lets water in, and it is easy to see from a ladder.

broan-634.title: Black Steel Roof Ventilation Cap
broan-634.description: Powder coated steel termination cap for range hood and bathroom extractor ductwork, incorporating a backdraft damper and integral bird screen.
about: This is the roof end of an exhaust run rather than a roof vent in the ventilation sense. A range hood, a bathroom fan or a rec room extractor has to discharge somewhere outside, and where the duct comes up through the roof this cap covers the hole, turns the air down and away, and keeps the weather out of the duct. Broan lists it for new work and for replacement alike. The cap turns the discharge downward so nothing blows back at the opening.

It takes either shape of duct that those fans use: rectangular 3 1/4 x 10 in, which is the standard behind a range hood, or round up to 8 in. The body is 24 gauge CRCQ steel, which is cold rolled commercial quality sheet, finished in black powder coat. The whole thing weighs about 4 lb and measures roughly 14 1/4 x 18 3/4 in across the base by 6 5/8 in tall. That is light enough to carry up a ladder in one hand while the other holds on.

Two things are built in. A backdraft damper hangs inside so that outside air, and the cold or heat that comes with it, cannot push back down the duct into the house when the fan is off. Both are already inside the cap when it comes out of the carton.

The one thing it must not be used for is a clothes dryer. Dryer exhaust carries lint, and lint packs against a damper and a screen until the run blocks and the lint itself becomes a fire load, which is why dryer terminations use a different cap with no screen. Broan states the restriction plainly. No wind rating or fire class is published, and Broan cover accessories for one year. Dryer caps use a wider throat and no screen for that reason.

master-flow-egv6ht.title: Gable Mount Attic Ventilator Fan
master-flow-egv6ht.description: Sixteen hundred cubic feet per minute behind the gable ventilation louver, with adjustable thermostat and humidistat prewired at the factory.

master-flow-prsolar2.title: Low Profile Solar Powered Attic Fan
master-flow-prsolar2.description: An integrated thirty five watt photovoltaic panel delivers seven hundred fifty cubic feet a minute, requiring absolutely no electrical wiring.
about: The argument for a solar attic fan is not really the electricity it saves, it is the wiring it avoids. There is no circuit to run into the attic, no switch, no breaker and no electrician, because the 35 watt panel is built into the unit and drives the motor directly. It moves up to 750 cubic feet a minute and Master Flow rates it for about 1,070 sq ft of attic floor. The panel and the fan are one unit, not two things to connect.

It is the low profile version, which matters more than it sounds. The whole unit is 28 x 28 in on plan and only 8 in tall, so it sits close to the slope instead of standing up off it like a domed solar vent, and the integral panel measures 17 1/2 in square. The housing is an impact resistant polymer in black rather than painted steel, so nothing on it rusts. A lower unit is also a unit that is harder to see from the street.

suntek-cma1919.title: Fixed Curb Mount Skylight Dome
suntek-cma1919.description: Polycarbonate double dome skylight wrapped in decorative aluminum, capping a site built curb of approximately twenty inches along each side.
about: A curb mount skylight does not flash itself into the roof. The curb is built on site out of timber, flashed like any other penetration, and the skylight then drops over the top of it as a lid. That division of labour is the reason the type survives: the waterproofing is ordinary roofing work that any roofer already knows, and the glazing unit is simply a cap. Nothing about the skylight itself has to keep water out on its own.

The glazing is polycarbonate rather than acrylic, and that is the specification worth noticing. Sun-Tek put polycarbonate at around thirty times the impact resistance of acrylic, which is what makes the type usual in hail country and in hurricane country. It is UV stabilized so the sheet does not yellow, and it comes as a double dome, bronze outside over clear inside. The bronze tint is what cuts the glare in a south facing room.

Two domes rather than one is insulation. The air trapped between the outer and inner sheets is what stops the unit running with condensation on a cold morning and what keeps some of the summer heat out of the room below. Around the outside the unit is wrapped in a decorative aluminum ring, and the corners of the frame are TIG welded rather than screwed. steeldash-tube-14ga-2in.title: Galvanized Steel Structural Tube
steeldash-tube-14ga-2in.description: Heavier gauge square steel section, two inches across, supplied in twenty four foot lengths for roofing frameworks and supporting structures.
about: This is plain structural stock rather than a roofing product: a hollow square steel section, 2 in on each face, sold in 24 ft lengths. It is what a carport frame, a patio cover, a purlin run over an outbuilding or a rack of solar rails gets built from, and it is the reason a metal roof over an open structure needs nothing else underneath it to span. None of it is specific to roofing, which is exactly the point of plain stock.

The gauge is the number that matters. At 14 gauge the wall is a nominal 0.083 in, which is the heavier end of what is sold as light structural tube and noticeably stiffer than the 16 and 18 gauge sections used for gates and handrails. A 2 in square section at that wall runs about 2.16 lb to the foot, so a full 24 ft length weighs roughly 51.8 lb. That is worth knowing before anyone tries to carry a full length up a ladder.

It is galvanized rather than painted or left black, and for anything that lives outdoors under a roof that is the distinction worth paying for. Zinc protects the cut faces and the drilled holes sacrificially, so a frame does not start rusting from the ends and the fixings the way bare hot rolled tube does once the first winter arrives. Zinc keeps on working at a scratch or a saw cut, which is the one thing paint cannot do.

Steeldash publish the size, the gauge and the length for this section and nothing further.
